PHYSICS — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #10
====

GRADE: Grade 10
SUBJECT: PHYSICS
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Moments and equilibrium? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Moments and equilibrium.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Moments and equilibrium.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Moments and equilibrium.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Moments and equilibrium.

2. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 50 °C
   B. 100 °C
   C. 37 °C
   D. 0 °C

3. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only carbon dioxide
   B. Nitrogen gas only
   C. Glucose and oxygen
   D. Only water vapour

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Introduction to Physics? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Introduction to Physics.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Introduction to Physics.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Introduction to Physics.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Introduction to Physics.

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Introduction to Electronics? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Introduction to Electronics.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Introduction to Electronics.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Introduction to Electronics.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Introduction to Electronics.

6. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Ice melting to water
   B. Iron rusting
   C. Paper burning to ash
   D. Milk souring

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Mechanical Properties of Materials? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Mechanical Properties of Materials.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Mechanical Properties of Materials.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Mechanical Properties of Materials.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Mechanical Properties of Materials.

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Current Electricity Measurement of current, e.m.f., potential difference and res? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Current Electricity Measurement of current, e.m.f., potential difference and res.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Current Electricity Measurement of current, e.m.f., potential difference and res.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Current Electricity Measurement of current, e.m.f., potential difference and res.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Current Electricity Measurement of current, e.m.f., potential difference and res.

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Pressure? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Pressure.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Pressure.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Pressure.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Pressure.

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Greenhouse Effect and Climate Change? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Greenhouse Effect and Climate Change.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Greenhouse Effect and Climate Change.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Greenhouse Effect and Climate Change.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Greenhouse Effect and Climate Change.

11. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water always increases oxygen
   B. Petrol fires have no fuel
   C. Water removes heat too quickly
   D. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

12. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   B. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   C. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   D. A mixture always has a fixed melting point

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Introduction to Space Physics and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Introduction to Physics and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Pressure and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Mechanical Properties of Materials and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
